Weak infants were reportedly rejected. Sparta produced the most feared soldiers in Greece and organized nearly all of life around the state rather than the household.

blocks.t: Sparta suffered oliganthropia — a collapse in the number of full citizens. Sources record about 8,000 Spartiates in 480 BC; when Aristotle wrote the Politics in the 330s he counted fewer than 1,000, and roughly 700 were fielded at Leuctra in 371 BC. Aristotle named the crisis and criticised Spartan handling of women, inheritance and land.

An honest caution about the cause. Historians attribute the collapse chiefly to land concentrating in fewer hands — men who could not pay their mess dues lost citizenship — together with war losses, the 464 BC earthquake, and families limiting heirs to avoid dividing estates. The agoge is not the cause scholars identify. What Sparta does show is a society that organised everything around the state rather than the household and could not replace itself. Worth noticing without overclaiming it.

de: Confucius taught that xiao — reverence for parents and ancestors — is the root of all virtue, and that a well-ordered society grows outward from a well-ordered home. Government legitimacy itself was framed in family terms. The teaching spread across China, Korea, Japan, and Vietnam.

blocks.t: East Asian societies built on this foundation have shown extraordinary continuity, high household stability, and multigenerational care of the elderly across more than two thousand years and many changes of dynasty and government.
Heavenly Father planted the fifth commandment in Chinese soil twenty-five centuries before missionaries arrived. Honor your parents is not a Western idea. It appears to be written on the human heart.

t: Rome Tries to Legislate Marriage Back
de: Alarmed by falling birth rates, widespread divorce, and childlessness among the Roman elite, Caesar Augustus enacted the Lex Julia and later the Lex Papia Poppaea. These laws penalized the unmarried and childless in matters of inheritance, rewarded parents of three or more children, and criminalized adultery. Rome attempted to restore the family by statute.

blocks.t: The laws were widely evaded, resented, and largely ineffective. Elite Roman fertility continued to fall. The historian Tacitus noted the futility. Rome went on producing law after law on the family for centuries without reversing the trend.

Rome discovered what modern nations are rediscovering: a legislature can subsidize and penalize, but it cannot manufacture the desire to marry and raise children. That grows in hearts and homes, not statutes.

de: In the Roman world, unwanted newborns — disproportionately daughters and the disabled — were legally exposed, left outside to die or be taken. Under patria potestas the father held legal power over the life of his household. Christians refused the practice from the earliest period, condemned it in the Didache, and are documented rescuing and adopting abandoned infants. Christian communities also forbade abortion, opposed easy divorce, and elevated the status of wives and widows.

blocks.t: Because Christians did not expose their daughters, their communities had a more balanced sex ratio and a higher natural growth rate than the surrounding population. Sociologist Rodney Stark identified this as one significant factor in how a small movement grew into the empire. Roman law moved against infanticide during the fourth century, though historians debate the dating and reach of specific statutes.

The early Christians did not win the Roman world by argument alone. They won it in part by keeping their babies. Faithful families are not only a private blessing — they are the way truth travels through time.

de: Medieval canon law, systematized in the Decretum of Gratian and refined over the following century, established that a valid marriage required the free consent of both the man and the woman. Neither a father nor a lord could validly marry off a daughter against her will. The Church made consent the essence of the bond.

blocks.t: This principle spread across Christendom and became the foundation of Western marriage law. It gave women a legal standing in the formation of the household that had not existed in most of the ancient world, and it made the couple — not the clan or the sovereign — the origin of the family.
Agency is the heart of Heavenly Father's plan, and it turned out to be the heart of marriage too. A covenant that is not freely chosen is not a covenant.

de: Martin Luther, an excommunicated Augustinian monk, married Katharina von Bora, a former nun. The marriage was a deliberate theological statement: that ordinary married family life is a holy calling equal to any monastic vocation. Their household in the Black Cloister — six children, students at the table, Katharina managing farm, brewery, and boarding house — became the prototype of the Protestant parsonage.

blocks.t: Across Protestant Europe, the married clergy household became a visible model of family life at the center of the community, and a documented engine of literacy, education, and civic leadership for centuries.
Luther taught that changing a diaper in faith is holier than the finest monastic devotion offered without it. That is the same doctrine that makes an ordinary bedtime story sacred work.

de: The Council of Trent issued the decree Tametsi, requiring that a valid marriage be contracted publicly before a priest and witnesses and entered in a parish register. Clandestine marriage — a private exchange of promises with no record — had been valid for centuries and was widely used to seduce and then abandon women, who had no proof of the union.

blocks.t: Marriage became a public, recorded, accountable act across Catholic Europe. Parish registers created the first systematic record of families, which is the reason family history research in Europe is possible at all before the modern era.
The records Trent created are the very records that FamilySearch volunteers index today so that families can be sealed. A decree in 1563 is still turning the hearts of children to their fathers.

t: The Slave Trade Breaks Families by Law
de: Across the Atlantic slave system, the marriages of enslaved people held no legal standing. Spouses and children could be sold apart at the owner's discretion, and were. Enslaved people married in their own communities anyway — often with vows adapted to say until death or distance do us part — knowing the law would not protect them.

blocks.t: After emancipation, freedpeople placed thousands of Information Wanted advertisements in newspapers searching for spouses, parents, and children sold away decades earlier, and formalized marriages in enormous numbers as soon as it became legally possible. Many searched for the rest of their lives and never found them.

When people who had every legal reason to abandon family instead spent their freedom searching for it, they revealed something permanent about human beings. The bond is not a social construct. It survived a system engineered to destroy it.

meta: Weakened the Family · Britain and Industrializing West
de: Industrialization moved work out of the home and into the mill and mine. Children as young as five worked twelve to sixteen hour shifts. Fathers, mothers, and children were separated for most of waking life. Households crowded into cities faster than housing, sanitation, or schools could follow.

blocks.t: Child mortality, illiteracy, and family breakdown rose sharply in the new industrial districts. The public response came slowly: factory acts, compulsory schooling, and eventually the abolition of child labor in the industrialized world.

The Industrial Revolution created enormous prosperity and nearly consumed the households that produced the workers. Every economy eventually learns it cannot spend down the family faster than the family can renew it.

de: With emancipation, formerly enslaved people gained the legal right to marry and to keep their children. Freedmen's Bureau agents recorded marriages by the tens of thousands in the first years alone. Newspapers filled with advertisements from people searching for family members sold away years or decades before.

blocks.t: Black households formed and held at high rates through Reconstruction and well into the twentieth century, under conditions of severe poverty and legal discrimination. Historians studying census records have documented that the great majority of Black children lived in two-parent homes for generations after slavery.
Given the barest legal permission, people rebuilt families under crushing conditions. The desire to be a family is not fragile. What is fragile is a society that stops protecting it.

meta: Weakened the Family · Carlisle, Pennsylvania and across North America
de: Beginning with the Carlisle Indian Industrial School in 1879, governments in the United States and Canada removed Native and Indigenous children from their families to distant boarding schools, often by force. The stated philosophy was to kill the Indian and save the man. Children were forbidden their languages, separated from siblings, and kept from parents for years.

blocks.t: Generations were left without the experience of being parented, and without the languages and practices that carried their identity. Extensive documentation of abuse, unmarked graves, and multigenerational trauma has followed. Both nations have since issued formal apologies.

This was done by people who sincerely believed they were helping. That is the warning. Whenever a program requires separating children from parents to achieve its good intentions, the good intentions are not enough.

de: The Bolsheviks set out to dissolve what they considered bourgeois marriage. The 1918 Family Code made divorce available at the request of either spouse without grounds, removed all legal distinction between children born inside and outside marriage, and stripped marriage of religious character. In 1920 Soviet Russia became the first nation on earth to legalize abortion on request, free of charge. Theorists such as Alexandra Kollontai promoted free union as the proletarian replacement for marriage. The state expected the family to wither away.

blocks.t: Divorce rates soared. Moscow statisticians reported roughly three abortions for every live birth. An estimated seven million besprizorniki — homeless, parentless street children — were roaming the country by 1922. The birth rate fell. Officials grew alarmed at family disintegration and labor shortage.

This is the closest thing history offers to a controlled experiment. A government deliberately removed the supports around marriage and recorded what happened. What happened was millions of abandoned children.

meta: A Society Reversed Course · Moscow, Soviet Union
de: The Soviet state enacted the law On the Protection of Motherhood and Childhood. Abortion was banned. Divorce was made difficult and expensive. Cash bonuses were introduced for mothers of many children, along with expanded maternity leave, childcare, and clinics. The published draft stated its purpose plainly: combating light-minded attitudes towards the family and family obligations.

blocks.t: Soviet jurists who had taught that law and the family would wither away were condemned for legal nihilism; several were arrested and shot. The regime that had set out to abolish the family spent the rest of its existence trying to rebuild it. Historians record the motive as falling birth rates and the aim of strengthening the family unit as a bulwark of social stability.

An officially atheist state, with no interest in scripture and every ideological reason to persist, examined its own results and concluded that the family is a bulwark of social stability. Sometimes the strongest witness for a truth is an opponent forced to admit it.

de: During the Cultural Revolution, Chinese youth were mobilized as Red Guards and encouraged to denounce teachers, elders, and their own parents as class enemies. Loyalty to the Party was placed explicitly above loyalty to family. Households were divided, children were sent to the countryside, and public struggle sessions were conducted by young people against their own relatives.

blocks.t: An estimated generation of education was lost, temples and ancestral records were destroyed, and countless families were permanently fractured. China has spent decades since attempting to restore filial and social cohesion, including a 2013 law requiring adult children to visit their aging parents.

Confucius had taught China for 2,400 years that reverence for parents is the root of virtue. When that root was deliberately cut, the society did not become freer. It became something the country is still recovering from.

t: Angkar Is Your Mother and Father
de: The Khmer Rouge separated children from parents into work brigades, arranged mass forced marriages between strangers, and taught that Angkar — the Organization — had replaced family entirely. Children were trained to report their parents. Family meals and private households were abolished in favor of communal eating.

blocks.t: Roughly 1.7 to 2 million people died, close to a quarter of the population. Survivors describe the destruction of family bonds as among the deepest and longest-lasting injuries, persisting long after the regime fell.
Every regime that has tried to replace the family with itself has ended in mass graves or demographic collapse, and often both. The pattern has no exceptions.

de: China limited most families to a single child, enforced through fines, job loss, and in many documented cases coerced abortion and sterilization. Combined with a traditional preference for sons and the arrival of ultrasound, the policy produced widespread sex-selective abortion and abandonment of infant girls.

blocks.t: China now has tens of millions more young men than young women. The 4-2-1 problem emerged, in which one working adult may support two parents and four grandparents. China recorded its first population decline in decades and its fertility rate is now among the lowest in the world.
A policy designed to solve a crisis of too many people created a crisis of too few — and cost a generation of daughters. Central planners can count people. They cannot see families.

t: China Reverses and Begins Paying for Babies
de: China ended the one-child policy in 2015, moved to a two-child policy, then a three-child policy in 2021, and has since introduced cash subsidies, extended parental leave, tax incentives, housing benefits, and restrictions on the private tutoring industry that made child-rearing expensive.

blocks.t: Births have continued to fall despite the incentives. The same state that spent thirty-five years preventing births now struggles to encourage them.
It is far easier for a government to stop families from forming than to persuade them to form again. The damage is fast. The repair is generational.

meta: Complex Effect · California and across the United States
de: California enacted the first no-fault divorce law in 1969, allowing a marriage to be dissolved without proving wrongdoing. Every American state adopted some form of it over the following sixteen years. The reform was widely supported as a humane escape from adversarial proceedings and from abusive marriages.

blocks.t: The American divorce rate roughly doubled between the mid-1960s and 1980 before declining again from the 1990s onward. Researchers continue to disagree about how much of the rise the law caused and how much reflected broader cultural change already underway. Research generally finds reduced rates of domestic violence and female suicide in states that adopted it, alongside significant increases in children living apart from a parent.

This one is genuinely complicated and it is dishonest to pretend otherwise. Some marriages should end, and some people were rescued. And a great many children experienced a loss that no policy intended and none can undo.

meta: Weakened the Family · United States and much of the West
de: In 1960 roughly five percent of American births were to unmarried mothers. That figure now stands around forty percent. Roughly one in four American children lives in a home without a father present. Similar trends have appeared across much of the Western world.

blocks.t: Children raised without a father present show, on average and after controlling for income, higher rates of poverty, incarceration, school dropout, teen pregnancy, and mental health difficulty. Researchers debate how much is caused by father absence itself versus poverty and other factors that accompany it, but the association is one of the most consistently replicated findings in family social science.
Fathers are not optional and they are not interchangeable with a check. This is not a judgment on any single mother doing heroic work. It is a plea to build a culture where fathers stay.

meta: Weakened the Family · Worldwide, concentrated in East Asia and Europe
de: South Korea recorded a total fertility rate of 0.72 in 2023, the lowest ever measured for a nation, with Seoul at 0.55. Replacement level is 2.1. Japan, Italy, Spain, Taiwan, Singapore, and China are all far below replacement, and the United States is below it as well. South Korea has spent more than 360 trillion won since 2006 attempting to reverse the trend.

blocks.t: The money has not worked. The OECD projects that pension, health, and long-term care costs in Korea will more than double to over seventeen percent of GDP by 2060. Korean officials and press now openly use the phrase national extinction. Governments across the developed world are discovering that subsidies alone do not produce children.

Augustus tried it with Roman law. Stalin tried it with bonuses and bans. Korea has tried it with hundreds of billions. No civilization has ever successfully paid its way out of a family collapse. Families are not built by policy. They are built by people who believe the work is worth doing.

de: The Fair Labor Standards Act set federal minimum ages for employment and effectively ended widespread child labor in the United States, completing a reform movement that had been building for decades alongside compulsory education laws.

blocks.t: Children returned from the factory to the school and the home. Literacy rose, child mortality fell, and childhood itself became a protected stage of life rather than a brief prelude to labor.

For most of history, children were small workers. The idea that a child should be raised, taught, played with, and read to at night is a hard-won inheritance. Bedtime stories are a privilege that was fought for.

de: Confucius teaches filial piety - that honor to parents and ancestors is the foundation of all virtue. The family is the basic unit of society and the parent-child relationship is sacred.

blocks.t: The Fifth Commandment. The Family Proclamation. The spirit of Elijah turning hearts of children to fathers. Heavenly Father placed the same family truth in Chinese culture that He gave Israel on Mount Sinai.

Over 1.5 billion people today live in cultures shaped by Confucian family values. Heavenly Father planted the doctrine of eternal families in Chinese culture 2500 years before Latter-day Saint missionaries arrived.

meta: Buddhist - South and East Asia · India, Nepal, China, Southeast Asia
de: Siddhartha Gautama teaches that compassion for all living beings is the highest virtue. Suffering can be overcome through wisdom and right living. The impermanence of worldly things points to a deeper reality.

blocks.t: Christ taught: be ye therefore merciful as your Father also is merciful. Compassion as the highest virtue is one of the deepest gospel truths Heavenly Father planted across Asia.

Buddhism spread literacy, ethical teaching, and the concept of inner spiritual cultivation across Asia - preparing hundreds of millions of hearts for the gospel's deeper truths about compassion and eternal life.

de: Shinto teaches profound gratitude for the gifts of creation, the importance of ritual purity and cleanliness, and reverence for the divine in the natural world. Every aspect of life is sacred.

blocks.t: The gospel teaches that the earth and all creation are Heavenly Father's gift. Gratitude, purity, and reverence are gospel virtues. Japan's culture of cleanliness and careful attention to beauty reflects these seeds.

When the gospel reached Japan Latter-day Saint missionaries found a people whose culture of gratitude, purity, and family reverence was deeply compatible with gospel living. Japan today has hundreds of thousands of Latter-day Saints.

meta: Hindu - Indian subcontinent · India, Nepal, Southeast Asia
de: Despite its polytheistic surface, Hindu philosophy contains a profound monotheistic core - Brahman, the one supreme reality underlying all existence. Atman - the individual soul - is real and eternal. Karma reflects the law of justice. Dharma reflects moral duty.

blocks.t: The Hindu concept of an eternal soul, divine justice, and moral duty echoes gospel truths about the eternal nature of intelligences, the law of justice requiring an Atonement, and the duty to serve others.

India has been a land of intense spiritual seeking for 3500 years. Heavenly Father placed truths about the eternal soul and divine justice in Indian philosophy that prepared seeking hearts for the fullness of the gospel.

de: Zoroaster teaches that existence is a cosmic battle between Ahura Mazda (the Wise Lord of light and truth) and Ahriman (the spirit of darkness and lies). Humans must choose good thoughts good words and good deeds. The righteous will be resurrected.

blocks.t: The Book of Mormon teaches that we must choose liberty and eternal life through the great Mediator or captivity and death through the devil. The cosmic conflict between light and darkness is a foundational gospel truth.

Zoroastrianism influenced Judaism during the Babylonian captivity introducing concepts of angels Satan resurrection and final judgment that appear in the later books of the Old Testament. Heavenly Father used one culture to prepare another.

meta: Egyptian - Ancient Egypt · Egypt, North Africa
de: Ancient Egypt was deeply preoccupied with life after death - the soul's journey the judgment of the heart against a feather of truth and resurrection. The concept that the physical body would be restored and that moral choices in this life determine the next life.

blocks.t: The gospel teaches resurrection as a gift to all through Christ's Atonement and judgment according to works. Egypt placed these truths in culture 2000 years before Moses. Abraham knew these truths when he visited Egypt.

The Egyptian understanding of afterlife judgment and resurrection - however distorted over centuries - preserved a cultural memory of truths about eternal life that Heavenly Father had placed in early human civilization.

t: African Traditional: God the Creator Father
de: Across hundreds of African traditional cultures there is a remarkably consistent belief in a supreme Creator God - often called by names meaning Father or Great One - who is good just and the source of all life. Below this high God are lesser spiritual beings.

blocks.t: The Supreme Being in African traditional religion is often described as Father Creator and Judge - attributes Heavenly Father revealed in the Restoration. These cultures preserved knowledge of the Eternal Father across millennia.

African traditional religions preserve a memory of the Creator Father that missionaries consistently found prepared African converts to understand the Restoration's revelation of Heavenly Father. Africa has the fastest-growing Latter-day Saint population in the world.

t: Greek Philosophy: The Logos and Divine Reason
meta: Greek Philosophy - Stoicism and Platonism · Greece, Mediterranean
de: Greek philosophers teach that a divine Logos - a rational principle underlying all existence - orders the universe. Plato argues for the immortality of the soul and eternal Forms of truth beauty and goodness that exist beyond the physical world.

blocks.t: John 1:1 opens: In the beginning was the Word (Logos) and the Word was with God. Greek philosophy prepared the Mediterranean world to receive Christ's identity as the divine Logos made flesh.

The koine Greek language and Platonic philosophical vocabulary were the tools the New Testament writers used to articulate Christ's divine nature. Heavenly Father prepared Greek thought as the intellectual vessel for the gospel's spread.

meta: Stoic Philosophy - Roman Empire · Rome, Mediterranean
de: Stoic philosophers teach that all human beings share a common rational nature and are therefore brothers. Virtue is the only true good. External circumstances cannot destroy inner peace. Live according to nature and reason.

blocks.t: Paul's letters to the Romans and Corinthians use Stoic vocabulary and concepts to explain gospel truths. The Stoic concept of universal brotherhood prepared the Roman world for Paul's declaration that in Christ there is neither Jew nor Greek.

The Stoic concept of universal human brotherhood - radical for the ancient world where slaves were property - prepared Roman culture for the gospel's declaration of equal worth before Heavenly Father. Paul built on Stoic foundations.

meta: Celtic Christian - Ireland, Scotland, Wales · Ireland, Scotland, Wales, Brittany
de: Celtic Christianity preserves a unique vision of creation as sacred - a thin place where the divine and physical worlds are close. Every person bears the image of God. Creation itself is a form of revelation. Community and hospitality are sacred duties.

blocks.t: The gospel teaches that the earth was created as Heavenly Father's gift and that every human being is literally His child bearing His image. Celtic Christianity preserved these truths through the early medieval period.

Celtic monks like Columba and Patrick preserved Christianity in Ireland during the collapse of Rome - keeping the light of faith alive in the British Isles during the Dark Ages. From Ireland missionaries later re-evangelized much of Europe.

meta: Olmec, Maya, Aztec - Mesoamerica · Mexico, Guatemala, Honduras
de: Across Mesoamerican cultures spanning thousands of years the figure of the Feathered Serpent (Quetzalcoatl/Kukulkan) appears - a divine being associated with creation knowledge wind and the morning star. Some accounts describe him as light-skinned arriving from the east and promising to return.

blocks.t: The Book of Mormon records Christ's appearance to the Nephites in 34 AD. Latter-day Saint scholars have noted that widespread Mesoamerican traditions of a divine white-robed teacher who came from the east may preserve a cultural memory of this visit.

Whether or not Quetzalcoatl legends connect to Christ's visit they show that Heavenly Father placed a memory of divine visitation in multiple Mesoamerican cultures. These peoples were prepared to receive the Book of Mormon's record of Christ's appearance.

meta: Indigenous North America - many nations · North America
de: Across hundreds of Native American nations there is a remarkably consistent belief in a Great Spirit - a supreme Creator who is the source of all life and who is good. Ceremonies of gratitude prayer and harmony with creation reflect this foundational belief.

blocks.t: The Great Spirit of Native American tradition is described with attributes remarkably consistent with Heavenly Father - Creator Judge loving Father source of all good. These are seeds Heavenly Father planted in every nation and kindred and tongue.

When the gospel reached Native American communities missionaries consistently found that the concept of a supreme Creator Father required little explanation. The seeds were already there. Heavenly Father had never left His children without witnesses.

meta: Andean - Inca and pre-Inca cultures · Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador
de: The Andean Creator God Viracocha is described across pre-Inca and Inca cultures as the supreme Creator who made the sun moon stars and humanity. Some accounts describe him as weeping for his people - a God who loves and feels sorrow for His children.

blocks.t: Moses 7:28-29 records that Heavenly Father wept when shown the wickedness of the earth. A Creator God who weeps for His children is a deeply scriptural truth. Heavenly Father placed this revelation of His loving nature in Andean culture.

The Andean image of a weeping Creator who loves His people was placed in South American culture long before Christian missionaries arrived. When the gospel came it deepened and completed truths already present.

meta: Maori and Polynesian - Pacific · New Zealand, Polynesia
de: The most sacred level of Maori and Polynesian religious tradition - known only to the highest priests - contains the concept of Io the supreme God. Io is eternal the source of all life the God of light and truth who stands above all other spiritual beings.

blocks.t: Io in Maori tradition is described as eternal uncreated the source of light and the father of all - attributes that map remarkably onto Heavenly Father as revealed in the Restoration. This was a secret preserved among the highest priests.

When Latter-day Saint missionaries arrived in New Zealand in 1854 they found a people who already held - in their highest sacred tradition - a concept of a supreme eternal Father God. The seeds had been planted long before the missionaries arrived.

t: Universal: The Flood in Every Culture
de: The story of a great flood surviving family and divine rescue appears in over 200 cultures worldwide - Sumerian Babylonian Hindu Chinese Mesoamerican Native American Australian Aboriginal. The details differ but the core narrative is strikingly consistent.

blocks.t: Genesis 6-9 records Noah's flood as historical. The preservation of this story across cultures that had no contact with each other is evidence that they all descended from the same event and the same family. We are all Noah's children.

The universality of flood narratives is one of the most powerful evidences that humanity shares a common ancestor and a common sacred history. Heavenly Father preserved the memory of His dealings with Noah across every people on earth.

de: Every major religious and ethical tradition in human history contains a version of the Golden Rule - treat others as you would wish to be treated. Confucius 500 BC. Buddhism 500 BC. Hinduism 800 BC. Judaism 50 BC. Christianity 30 AD. Islam 620 AD.

blocks.t: Christ taught: Do unto others as you would have them do unto you. This is the law and the prophets. The fact that this principle appears independently in every major tradition worldwide is evidence that Heavenly Father placed it in the moral intuition of all His children.

The universal presence of the Golden Rule across cultures with no contact with each other is Heavenly Father's fingerprint on human moral intuition. He never left His children without this seed of truth.
